entities.name: PMID:27510244
observations: Retrospective pre/post cohort across 70 Cape Town TB clinics compared daily DOT with an integrated TB-HIV adherence model.
The model used 2 weeks of DOT and treatment-literacy sessions, then self-administered TB treatment with weekly community-care-worker home visits and HIV-care support.
Among 11,896 pre-intervention and 11,314 post-intervention patients, treatment success was 82.8% versus 82.5%; adjusted OR 1.02 (95% CI 0.89–1.17).
Default and death did not differ significantly; ART initiation increased from 67% to 74% (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.01–1.85).

entities.name: PMID:21276302
observations: Interrupted time-series study in five intervention and five comparison South African clinics evaluated lay-health-worker TB adherence support against DOT/usual care.
The intervention found no significant difference in TB cure or treatment success, with a small improvement in smear conversion and potential for improved TB-ART integration.

entities.name: Cape Town TB-HIV model
observations: In eligible drug-sensitive TB patients, structured community support maintained treatment success relative to routine daily DOT while increasing ART initiation.
The model de-intensified rather than eliminated supervision because it retained initial DOT; evidence does not establish superiority or universal replacement.
